title: Fix Unicode prefix matching in the Dag list
body:
Searching the Dag list for `카페` can omit `카페매출집계` on PostgreSQL with libc `en_US.utf8` collation. The code-point-derived upper bound does not follow the database's collation order.

Use substring equality for non-ASCII display-name prefixes. ASCII prefixes and other prefix filters retain their existing behavior. Update the API description to document the exception.

### Before / After

Searching for `카페` returns no results before the fix and correctly returns `카페매출집계` after the fix.

| AS-IS | TO-BE |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: no matching Dags](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ehddnr301/airflow/d93996cf892b223d23193cc64cb08f4315de122c/before.png) | ![After: matching Dag found](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ehddnr301/airflow/d93996cf892b223d23193cc64cb08f4315de122c/after.png) |

Captured from the local UI using the same synthetic data and PostgreSQL `en_US.utf8` collation. The before capture uses the original range matcher; the after capture uses substring equality.

In a warm-cache benchmark with 20,000 synthetic Dags, the sum of median count and list query times increased by approximately 3–5 ms. This avoids database-specific collation handling.

Validation:
- Core API/Always and common.compat/FAB tests, with and without DB access.
- PostgreSQL 16 regression and API cases: 9 passed.
- UI tests: 1,865 passed; SimpleAuth UI: 1 passed.
- Generated Python API client tests: 360 passed.
- Pre-commit/manual checks and affected documentation builds passed.

The remaining shared prefix matcher work is tracked separately.

related: #74551

         that back. It is an equality and not ``LIKE 'lower%'`` so it resolves under the same
         collation as the bounds — ``LIKE`` is case-insensitive on SQLite and MySQL ``_ci``
         columns, and would keep leaking case variants.
+
+        The upper bound is dropped when its bumped character is non-ASCII: the next code point
+        does not follow collation order there (PostgreSQL ``en_US.utf8`` sorts ``'카페매출집계'``
+        after ``'카펙'``), so the bound would exclude real matches.
         """
         clauses: list[ColumnElement[bool]] = [column >= lower]
-        if upper is not None:
+        if upper is not None and upper[-1].isascii():
             clauses.append(column < upper)
         clauses.append(func.substr(column, 1, len(lower)) == lower)
         return clauses

@@ -556,6 +576,29 @@ def test_only_values_with_the_prefix_come_back(self, select_names, term, expecte
         assert select_names(term) == expected
 
 
+@pytest.mark.db_test
+@pytest.mark.backend("postgres", "mysql")
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("term", "value"),
+    [
+        ("카페", "카페매출집계"),
+        ("café", "caféteria"),
+        ("카페a", "카페abc"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_prefix_search_matches_under_locale_collation(session, term, value):
+    if session.get_bind().dialect.name == "mysql":
+        collation = "utf8mb4_unicode_ci"
+    elif session.scalar(text("SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_collation WHERE collname = 'en_US.utf8')")):
+        collation = "en_US.utf8"
+    else:
+        pytest.skip("Requires the PostgreSQL en_US.utf8 collation")
+    column = literal(value, type_=String()).collate(collation)
+    param = _PrefixSearchParam(column).set_value(term)
+
+    assert session.scalars(param.to_orm(select(column))).all() == [value]
+
+
 class TestTaskDisplayNamePrefixPatternParam:
